$comment: Every source in the SCANNED TREES (packages/providers/**, packages/source-sdk/**) that emits a
snapshot — `SyncResult.presentExternalIds` or its structured twin `presentIds` — and how it
guarantees the snapshot is complete.
A snapshot is the source asserting that it has enumerated everything it holds, and the gateway
deletes whatever it stores that the assertion does not name. Emitting one from a read that
skipped a store, a repository, an account or a page is not reporting a smaller corpus; it is
ordering the deletion of the part that was not read. Withholding costs one cycle of deletion
detection. Emitting wrongly costs the corpus.
`snapshot-contract.test.ts` fails when a file in those trees emits a snapshot without a row here,
so a new source cannot ship one without someone writing down why it is safe. Adding a row is not
a rubber stamp: the sentence has to be true, and true of every path that reaches the emission.
What this file does NOT cover, and nothing here should be read as claiming otherwise: snapshot
emitters written in Swift or Kotlin (the phones push their own documents — Android call-log,
Android photos, iOS photos), and the synthetic twins under packages/providers-synth/. Neither is
reachable by a TypeScript scan of the two trees above.
`@omnesis/source-sdk`'s `SnapshotEnumeration` is the seam to build one through. It withholds by
default and only releases the ids when every discovered partition has been positively covered, so
a partition dropped by a bare `continue` holds the snapshot back rather than silently shrinking
it. Finalized incomplete reads emit snapshot-withheld issues; complete reassessments explicitly
clear them with issues: []. Intermediate pages and incremental ticks that do not reassess
enumeration leave issues omitted. Failed reads that throw instead already report sync failure.

emitters.packages/providers/apple/src/calendar.ts: One Calendar.sqlitedb. The page, count, signature and enumeration queries share `CALENDAR_EVENTS_FILTER` and the data-cutoff clause, so what counts as an indexable event cannot drift between them; the page additionally applies a cursor/watermark window (`membershipClause`) that the enumeration deliberately omits, since the enumeration must cover the whole store rather than this cycle's queue. A database that will not open returns before the snapshot with presentExternalIds explicitly undefined. It has no coverage floor of its own.
emitters.packages/providers/apple/src/call-log.ts: Bounded canonical day walk with a streamed content signature, restarting after drift; DISTINCT-day absence publishes only on the final stable page in a SQLite read transaction with the same filter and cutoff. Unavailable stores and partial reads never publish absence.
emitters.packages/providers/apple/src/contacts.ts: SnapshotEnumeration over every address book the scan discovered, readable or not, published as per-book claims. An address book that fails to open, or whose database file is not on disk yet, is a declared gap and is simply not claimed — the books that were read still vouch for themselves, and every document carries the book it came from so a claim is actionable. The signature is keyed per book and only a complete read advances it. Withholding is knowledge-based only: a complete read of a book that finds few or no contacts is claimed.
emitters.packages/providers/apple/src/imessage.ts: One chat.db, enumerated by a single full-table scan with no per-row skips. An open failure raises a typed SyncError; an absent store preserves the cursor and reports snapshot-withheld instead of producing an empty enumeration. Successful final scans clear the warning, including scans whose signature is unchanged.
emitters.packages/providers/apple/src/notes.ts: SnapshotEnumeration over the one note store. A schema whose column names cannot be identified fails the sync outright rather than filtering on a guess, which is what a macOS rename would otherwise do silently. Withholding is knowledge-based only: an enumeration that comes back small, or empty, is published — the source covered its partition and knows what the store holds, and a magnitude veto here would cancel a real deletion rather than delay it.
emitters.packages/providers/apple/src/voicemail.t: An unpaged full-table read; the snapshot is by construction the exact set of documents emitted. A malformed row throws rather than being skipped, and a database that will not open returns presentExternalIds explicitly undefined.
emitters.packages/providers/browser-history/src/i: Per-profile databases. The readers set `partialFailure` for zero profiles discovered, a profile database that will not open, and any per-profile query error; the source skips snapshot emission whenever it is set.
emitters.packages/providers/github/src/commits.ts: SnapshotEnumeration over the repositories the cycle opened with, frozen at cycle start so a listing that changes mid-cycle cannot add a partition nobody walked from the beginning. A repository is covered only by its listing reaching its last page; a permission or unknown error gaps it by name. A previously-synced repository absent from the accessible listing is the ledger's blind spot on its first absence — from there a revoked grant and a deletion are the same thing — and on its second is covered with no ids, which is how the two-strike rule sweeps it whether the cycle ends up snapshotting or claiming. Ids are added before the pending cap, so a capped lane does not shrink the enumeration. No magnitude test: an enumeration of zero commits where commits were known is published, since refusing it would cancel a real deletion instead of delaying it.
emitters.packages/providers/github/src/threads.ts: Same enumeration and frozen repository partitions as commits.ts, through repo-snapshot. A repository is covered only when its last discovery lane drains; failures gap it, and GraphQL null is a typed permission error rather than zero results. Only repeated permission failures on discussions settle as a disabled feature or absent grant; unknown, transient and network failures never become evidence of absence merely by repeating. Successful discovery clears the per-repository permission flag.
emitters.packages/providers/chrome/src/index.ts: One complete readable bookmark file. The tree is flattened and filtered by the same cutoff used for ingestion before publishing its exact URL set, including unchanged-checksum cycles. Malformed folder or URL nodes fail closed; absent files and invalid JSON retain the cursor without asserting presence. Empty valid files publish an empty snapshot. Repeated complete reads reconcile deletions even when the old knownIds cursor was lost.
SnapshotEnumeration over one notes partition during initial full backfill and daily unfiltered rewalks. Every eligible listed note is added before detail fetch, so a detail 404 retains its prior document and row rather than proving deletion. Presence for documents and analytics is emitted together only after the final list page. Invalid summaries, failed requests, missing or repeated continuation tokens, and page/item limits fail the page without advancing the cursor or asserting absence. An installed partial backfill without a ledger finishes without a snapshot, then starts a complete rewalk. A completed empty listing asserts empty presence in both planes.
emitters.packages/providers/google/src/calendar.t: The calendar list is followed to its last page and must be non-empty before the accumulated occurrence ids may reconcile — an account always owns its primary calendar, so an empty list is a failed read. A failed calendar drops the accumulator from the returned cursor.
emitters.packages/providers/imap/src/source.ts: SnapshotEnumeration over every selectable mailbox from a bounded, fail-closed LIST, each opened and enumerated 1..UIDNEXT-1 after the paged read has drained every mailbox and covered only once its own last page is in; a UIDVALIDITY that moved since that read makes that mailbox a declared gap, which withholds the account-wide form and re-queues that mailbox for bootstrap — every mailbox that moved is found in the one pass rather than one per cycle, and the cycle asserts nothing until they settle, because the page reporting them is not the last one, and any server omission — a metadata row missing from a requested page, an out-of-range or duplicate UID, an over-cap listing or scan — throws rather than shrinking the enumeration. Drafts, Junk, Trash and \Noselect mailboxes are excluded from ingestion and enumeration alike, so their absence names nothing the gateway stores. When attachment extraction is enabled, the same pass reconstructs every eligible attachment child id from BODYSTRUCTURE alone — the identical (filename, size, mime) gate and stable-id derivation the paged read extracts with — so a child document can never exist that the snapshot fails to name; a child named for an attachment whose extraction failed is a harmless missing entry, and a metadata reply missing its BODYSTRUCTURE throws rather than naming zero children. Disabling extraction stops naming children — the sweep then removes them, and re-enabling requires a resync to rebuild them. No magnitude test: a mailbox the operator emptied enumerates as empty and is published.
emitters.packages/providers/local-files/src/index: SnapshotEnumeration over configured folders canonicalised at creation, with bounded hashed partition keys for long paths. Failed directories, depth/entry/file ceilings and unreadable files without a trusted prior identity gap the affected root. A known unreadable file retains its last identity while readable siblings still reconcile. Placeholders, hardlinks and files caught mid-rewrite remain named. The cutoff filters ingestion, not presence. Claims are final-page only and withheld if that page contains documents from a gapped root. Files outside the configured scope are pruned only once every currently configured root was read; a missing configured mount retains unattributed entries rather than impersonating scope removal. Complete scans therefore resume whole-source snapshots after intentional scope removal. Legacy files are reread once to stamp their bounded root partition even when unchanged.
SnapshotEnumeration over discovered databases plus previously known databases absent from a complete discovery, closed through finishRewalk on every path to done. Retrieve/query failures, backoff, partial database objects and truncated row pagination gap their database. Partial row objects and cutoff-skipped live rows remain named on both planes. Incomplete discovery withholds whole-source presence and retirement claims, and its uncertainty survives cached discovery retries. Complete database reads publish document claims and per-table typed presence; removed databases publish empty claims and empty table snapshots even while a sibling is gapped. Retired names and empty table baselines remain in the size-limited cursor for repeated gateway corroboration until rediscovered; they are not an unbounded per-row history. Full rewalks re-emit unchanged summary documents to stamp legacy partitions. A reappearing database is removed from the retired inventory, and its fresh records/claims cancel pending absences.
emitters.packages/providers/notion/src/pages.ts: A search result that comes back partial sets `snapshotDirty` on the rewalk cursor and withholds the snapshot on completion; the id format is the same `page-<hyphenless>` form the documents carry.
The bounded re-walk publishes its enumeration once it has followed every page to the delta link, and a mid-walk delta expiry discards the accumulated set rather than reconciling from a partial one — completeness is what this source vouches for. It applies no magnitude test: a walk that comes back far smaller than the drive was known to be, or empty, is still published, because withholding would leave the gateway with no signal to mark and no deadline to run, and a drive the operator emptied would stay indexed permanently.
emitters.packages/providers/outlook/src/outlook-c: SnapshotEnumeration over the calendars the enumeration opened with, frozen when it began so a `/me/calendars` that changes under the cycle cannot add a calendar nobody walked; the queue is filtered to that same list, so a calendar the enumeration was not opened with is never walked. A calendar is covered only when its delta link arrives — the point at which it has been read in full — one this account cannot delta-query is a declared gap, and one that left the account mid-enumeration is emptied, because the listing says it holds nothing. The account-wide form is published only when every calendar was covered AND the calendar list was non-empty: an empty list is far likelier to be a transient read than an account that lost every calendar, and it withholds the claims too. Short of that the calendars read in full are emitted as `presentClaims` for the documents alone; the analytics rows have no per-partition form, so a claiming cycle sends no `presentIds` rather than telling the table those are all the rows there are.
emitters.packages/providers/strava/src/activities: A completed account rewalk lists activity IDs as document presence and typed presentKeys for all nine activity tables, with child tables reconciled by activity_id. Athlete and gear profile tables are left unchanged. Partial pages and failed enumeration assert no snapshot; a completed empty rewalk publishes empty presence for every activity table. The rewalk ends on a short page; gateway corroboration and deadlines protect against a one-off smaller upstream enumeration without cancelling intentional deletion.
emitters.packages/providers/things/src/index.ts: Both emit paths route through one SnapshotEnumeration over the single store, gapped when `probeThingsSchema` fails — the verdict is consulted, not merely logged, and re-probed while it is failing. Note the page query and the enumeration deliberately DIFFER: the page selects `type IN (0,1)` changed since the cursor with no `trashed` predicate, so a newly-trashed task is emitted as a change, while the enumeration adds `trashed = 0` so the same task is absent from the snapshot and reconciled away. That asymmetry is the deletion signal.
emitters.packages/source-sdk/src/local-agent-sess: SnapshotEnumeration over adapter roots. Failed directories, unresolved paths, caps and malformed transcripts without a trusted complete prior parse gap their root. A known unreadable transcript retains its last complete IDs while healthy sibling deletions reconcile; repeated I/O failures never prove absence. Missing optional roots are covered empty, missing required roots are gapped. Tree changes during pagination and documents from gapped roots withhold claims too. Complete scans prune vanished legacy entries and reread rootless surviving entries to stamp their root. Under newest-session duplicate selection, an unreadable sibling root retains vanished prior winners because they may have moved into that root; this prevents a live-to-archive move from temporarily deleting the session. Whole-source presence is published only when all roots are complete.
emitters.packages/source-sdk/src/source.ts: Not a source: `syncPage` is the generic SyncResult builder and passes its caller's `presentExternalIds` straight through, so the claim belongs to whoever calls it. Callers inside the scanned trees each have a row here. Callers OUTSIDE them do not: the synthetic twins under `packages/providers-synth/` are test doubles rather than sources and are covered by the E2E sweep instead.
emitters.packages/source-sdk/src/table-write.ts: Not a source: `normalizeTableKeys` collapses the two spellings of a write's row keys and hands back what its caller sent, so the claim belongs to whoever built the write. It cannot narrow or widen a snapshot — every key it returns came in, and a write naming rows both ways is refused rather than merged.
